Resolves #21564

The README's first screen now says what the repository is, shows it and offers a first step. The title names the engine and its builder. Two sentences follow, then a record of the 30 days to 20 Nov (pull requests, issues, reviews across model families, outside contributors), three rows of doors (build, run a team, contribute) and one large picture of DevIndex that opens the live app. Six linked covers of v14 examples and "The Engine" follow on the second screen. The lead cluster (label, ladder sentence, apex) opens the README's second part, word for word.

Evidence: L3 (GitHub's render of the pushed head, logged out, 1440 × 900) → L3 required (AC-1 and AC-2 judge the rendered page). No residuals.

Change class: zero-delta (`docs`). agent-preflight: not hosted here; lint-staged ran on both commits.
Prescription checked: `README.md` — owns the concern (the repository's page and npm's package page render this file; the org profile, the other candidate, does not exist).

## The decision in it

On 16 Oct the operator placed the label on top of the README (#19811). This pull request leads with the repository's own product and moves the lead cluster, intact and in its order, to the README's second part; ADR 0018 §2.3 gains the sentence. **His merge is the confirmation, as on #21420.** The label-first top that was read against it is quoted under `## Cold look`; restoring it is one commit.

## Cold look

One reader without session context per round (Explore, Sonnet), frames unlabelled, today's README as a blind control. Two visitors, ten seconds on a first screen each: **E**, a senior web engineer who followed "Neo.mjs 14 is out: a multi-threaded JavaScript application engine with grids, Gantt, scheduler and boards"; **C**, a CTO who followed "a team of AI agents from different labs that maintains a real codebase in public". Six questions per visitor and variant: what is this repository, does it match the link, a grade from 1 to 10 for "what do I get and what do I do next", go on or leave, the first click, the strongest objection.

| Round | Frames | Today | Label first | Engine first |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | local render, first draft | E 2, leaves · C 4 | E 5 · C 6 | E 8 · C 5 |
| 2 | local render, with the record line and doors per audience | E 2, leaves · C 4 | E 5 · C 6 | E 8 · C 7 |
| 3 | GitHub's render of `63d456fa72`: six covers, no DevIndex picture | E 2, leaves · C 4 | not read | E 7 · C 6 |
| 4 | GitHub's render of `9ffa23d84f`, the head: DevIndex above the covers | E 2, leaves · C 5 | not read | E 8 · C 7 |

Round 4 also asked whether the visitor would star the repository after two screens. Today: E no, C "maybe, lean no". The head: E yes, "as a shortlist bookmark"; C "maybe, lean yes".

**Round 4's reader disagrees with the DevIndex picture.** At README width it "reads as a spreadsheet": small text, no message, dark on dark, and it pushes the six covers, "currently the best evidence", one scroll down. The operator named DevIndex as the more impressive picture and also said one could call it too much for a cover. A model reads density differently from a person, so this stays his call: the picture leads as built, and putting the covers above it is one commit.

The label-first top read: H1 "An agent institution, and the engine it builds", then the ladder sentence, then "This repository is the engine that institution builds, reviews and maintains in public". Its reader as E: "Is this a UI product or an AI experiment? Every bold line is about agents." Its second screen then defined Neo.mjs a second time, as an application engine.

**The record's window** is the operator's choice of 20 Nov: the 30 days to that day, with both dates written out so the line ages well (`b130586013`; the earlier heads carried October). All numbers below are for the public repositories of the org, merged or closed from 21 Oct to 20 Nov 2026, read on 20 Nov.

**The first line.** 1,586 merged pull requests, 290 of them Dependabot's, so **1,296**; **1,467** closed issues. Both links on the line run the search.

**The second and third line** come from GitHub's GraphQL API over those 1,296 (`search` with `reviews` and `mergedBy` per pull request, in ranges of four days because a search returns at most 1,000):

| Who wrote it | Pull requests | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| AI maintainer accounts (ten merged in the window) | **1,177** | **1,125** carry a review in state `APPROVED` from a maintainer account of another model family (Claude: Ada, Grace, Vega, Mnemosyne, Clio; Gemini: Julia, Maryam; GPT: Euclid, Emmy, Sophie). **463** carry a review in state `CHANGES_REQUESTED` or `DISMISSED` from a peer |
| Outside accounts | **119** from **65** accounts | 103 in `neo`, 8 in the Brain, 4 in Skills, 3 in the Institution, 1 in `pages`; all approved by a maintainer |
| The operator | 0 | `mergedBy` is the operator on all 1,296 |

On "463 sent back": the first formal review of an AI-written pull request was an approval on 668, a change request on 456, and 51 merged with no formal review (71 of the window's AI-written pull requests are cover uploads in `pages`). In the engine repository alone it is 244 of 657. A five-day sample of the engine repository (16 to 20 Nov, 192 AI-written) found 94 with a formal change request and none whose change request stood only in a comment. The operator expects the share to be higher ("most get a change request in round one"); GitHub's review states do not show that, and the line carries what they show. The counting script is in the comments, for a reviewer to re-run.

## Evolution

The ticket's first shape kept the label on top and added the engine below it. Two blind reads graded that 5 and 6 and the engine-first top 8 and 7, so the placement changed and goes to the operator with the reads. The operator then read the pushed version: better, "but that was easy"; the DevIndex grid is the more impressive picture, and the README "clearly did not convert" while outside contributors arrived in numbers. That put DevIndex above the covers and gave contributors their own row of doors. Three more reads of his followed the same afternoon: no comparison with Ext JS on a front door; the record's window is the last 30 days with both dates, not October, because this is the project's peak; and the outside contributors of that window belong on the line.

<details>
<summary>The counting script (scratch; run with an authenticated <code>gh</code>: <code>node review-share.mjs 2026-10-01 2026-10-31</code>)</summary>

```js
import {execFileSync} from 'node:child_process';

const
    [from = '2026-10-01', to = '2026-10-31'] = process.argv.slice(2),
    family = {
        'neo-opus-ada'       : 'claude', 'neo-opus-grace': 'claude', 'neo-opus-vega': 'claude',
        'neo-fable-mnemosyne': 'claude', 'neo-fable-clio': 'claude',
        'neo-gemini-julia'   : 'gemini', 'neo-gemini-maryam': 'gemini',
        'neo-gpt-euclid'     : 'gpt', 'neo-gpt-emmy': 'gpt', 'neo-gpt-sophie': 'gpt',
        'neo-kimi-phoebe'    : 'kimi', 'neo-kimi-iris': 'kimi',
        'neo-preview'        : 'undisclosed'
    },
    query = `query($q: String!, $cursor: String) {
        search(query: $q, type: ISSUE, first: 100, after: $cursor) {
            issueCount
            pageInfo {hasNextPage endCursor}
            nodes {... on PullRequest {
                number title
                repository {nameWithOwner}
                author {login}
                mergedBy {login}
                reviews(first: 50) {nodes {author {login} state}}
            }}
        }
    }`;

function page(q, cursor) {
    const args = ['api', 'graphql', '-f', `query=${query}`, '-f', `q=${q}`];

    cursor && args.push('-f', `cursor=${cursor}`);

    return JSON.parse(execFileSync('gh', args, {maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024}).toString()).data.search
}

// A search returns at most 1,000 results, so the month is read in two halves.
function collect(start, end) {
    const
        q     = `org:neomjs is:public is:pr is:merged merged:${start}..${end} -author:app/dependabot`,
        nodes = [];

    let cursor = null, result;

    do {
        result = page(q, cursor);
        nodes.push(...result.nodes);
        cursor = result.pageInfo.endCursor
    } while (result.pageInfo.hasNextPage);

    if (nodes.length !== result.issueCount) {
        throw new Error(`${start}..${end}: read ${nodes.length} of ${result.issueCount}`)
    }

    return nodes
}

const
    month = from.slice(0, 8),
    prs   = [...collect(from, `${month}15`), ...collect(`${month}16`, to)],
    ai    = prs.filter(pr => family[pr.author?.login]),
    count = predicate => ai.filter(predicate).length,
    approvals = pr => pr.reviews.nodes.filter(review => review.state === 'APPROVED'),
    crossFamily = pr => approvals(pr).some(review => {
        const reviewer = family[review.author?.login];
        return reviewer && reviewer !== family[pr.author.login]
    }),
    mergers = {};

ai.forEach(pr => {
    const login = pr.mergedBy?.login || 'unknown';
    mergers[login] = (mergers[login] || 0) + 1
});

console.log(`window ${from}..${to}: ${prs.length} merged pull requests without Dependabot, ${ai.length} written by AI maintainer accounts`);
console.log(`  with an approving review from a maintainer of a different model family: ${count(crossFamily)}`);
console.log(`  with an approving review from the operator: ${count(pr => approvals(pr).some(review => review.author?.login === 'tobiu'))}`);
console.log(`  with any approving review: ${count(pr => approvals(pr).length > 0)}`);
console.log(`  with a review that requested changes at some point: ${count(pr => pr.reviews.nodes.some(review => review.state === 'CHANGES_REQUESTED'))}`);
console.log(`  merged by: ${Object.entries(mergers).sort((a, b) => b[1] - a[1]).map(([login, n]) => `${login} ${n}`).join(', ')}`);
console.log(`  titled as a revert: ${count(pr => /^revert\b/i.test(pr.title))}`);
console.log(`  without a cross-family approval, by repository: ${JSON.stringify(ai.filter(pr => !crossFamily(pr)).reduce((map, pr) => {
    map[pr.repository.nameWithOwner] = (map[pr.repository.nameWithOwner] || 0) + 1;
    return map
}, {}))}`);
```
